label: End of a length-9 input: last original token (r,k,b,g,j,p,n,s,z,e) or <DEL> when the first token is in {2,1,h,y,x,q,i,l,3,u,g,c}
explanation: Length-and-position unit. 94% of activation mass is in length-9 sequences and nearly all of it is on two steps: the last original token (t=8, about 46% of mass) and the <DEL> step (t=9, about 47%). Length-8 sequences make up the remaining ~6% at the same two positions. It essentially never fires in the copy phase (1 activation) or on earlier original steps. Which token is present gates it. At t=8 it fires mostly when the last token is r, k, b, g, j, p, n, s, z or e (r is strongest; the top examples are r at about 0.95 of max), and rarely when it is x, w, i, u or y. At <DEL> it depends on the token about to be output (orig(0)): it fires most for 2, 1, h, y, x, q, i, l, 3, u, g. Position alone, (L==9)&(t in {8,9}), gets dev mass recall 0.93 but precision only 0.34. The token-conditioned predicate raises dev F1 to 0.71 (precision 0.73, mass recall 0.83). The token sets are empirical lists and not one clean category, so the explanation is incomplete.
